builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Learning Conditional Expectation Operators via Functional Newton Updates
summary: FSNM replaces fixed-basis or RKHS-based estimation of conditional expectation operators with a basis-free, low-rank fit of the centered joint-to-product density ratio kernel, trained by alternating functional Newton updates implemented as boosted vector-valued regression trees. It costs an iterative stagewise boosting procedure with a preconditioned regression solved at each step, plus rank and weak-learner accuracy hyperparameters, and its guarantees are population-level rather than finite-sample. Evidence is limited to synthetic experiments; there are no benchmarks against established estimators on real data, no reported compute or latency measurements, and the global-optimality result assumes full centered L2 spaces and a relative weak-learner condition that the tree booster may not satisfy in practice, so the learned kernel may fail to capture the true spectral structure on real distributions.
rationale: This is a statistical operator-learning method validated only on synthetic data with theoretical rather than empirical performance claims, so it warrants monitoring rather than production adoption, and it does not address the reader's LLM-serving constraints.
technique: Functional spectral-Newton method for conditional expectation operators
